prereg_ambiguities.text: the addendum takes 'the larger of section 7's RL-val training-seed floor and the navtest seed floor', but section 7's training-seed row names TWO quantities (|R0d - R1d| constrained, |R0 - R1o| unconstrained) and does not say PDMS or TTC.  Read here: PDMS (E's unit), the larger of the two terms = bar L's PDMS F_seed; both terms are in the record.  Without R0 and R1o (RL-val reads) the floor cannot be built and clause 3 is unread: E reads NOT_READ unless REFUTED (which needs no floor).
prereg_ambiguities.where: addendum R4 / section 5 E clause 3 / section 7

prereg_ambiguities.text: 'the own-A vs C0-A difference is reported beside G as a disclosure': this tool is not given C0-A's u1000 dumps and does NOT compute it.  The G record carries disclosures.A-G2 = NOT_COMPUTED_BY_THIS_TOOL; the owner reports it beside G (section 7's 'same run again' floor, precedent R0-A vs C0-A PDMS +0.01 [-0.13, +0.14]).

'a K-MON kill applying the K3 rule counts as K3, judged by its recorded reason': the addendum gives no text for that reason.  Read here: the real monitor's K3 text 'g3/g5 bound breached at <tag> and <tag>' (rls1_checks.judge).  Any other recorded reason (the chain writes 'kill rules unenforceable: monitor died rc N' / 'not READY within Ns') is not the K3 rule, so the kill is O7.

'(3,000 sets / 75 logs)' is parenthetical: the addendum does not say a different pool is a refusal.  The G record carries the pool counts and `pool_matches_registered`; a mismatch is a note on the arm, not a NOT_READ.

the JOINT-resample pooled interval is the producer's (IMPL step 9); this tool cannot re-derive it from per-token data.  It checks the declaration (`pooled.resample == 'joint'`), `n_tokens == 12146`, `n_logs == 136` and that pooled.PDMS.mean is the mean of the two pairs' PDMS means; the interval itself is taken from the file.

'the same 2 x F_seed yardstick printed beside' the PDMS cost: F_seed is recomputed on the PDMS contrasts (its own unit); the TTC F_seed that decides L is printed beside it.  Neither moves the verdict.
